questions.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-{x}_{2}^{2}\le {x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

As a result,  

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & \le {x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So,  in turn, $Q(x)\le 1.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $1.$ But before we conclude that $1$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=1.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =(1)^{2}-(0)^{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the maximum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $1.$

questions.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=4{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
4{x}_{1}^{2}\ge 2{x}_{1}^{2},\,3{x}_{2}^{2}\ge 2{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =4{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge 2{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=2(1)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge 2.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $2.$ But before we conclude that $2$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=2.$

Notice that when  $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =4{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =4(0)^{2}+3(0)^{2}+2(1)^{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $2.$

questions.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=-{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}-1-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-1-\lambda )(2-\lambda )-4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-\lambda -6 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda -3) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =-2,\,3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
min\{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1\}=-2.
$$

questions.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=-4{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-3{x}_{2}^{2}\ge -4{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-4{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & \ge -4{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So,  

$$
\begin{aligned}-4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2})=-4(1)=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge -4.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $-4.$ But before we conclude that $-4$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=-4.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-4{x}_{1}^{2}-3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =-4(1)^{2}-3(0)^{2} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $-4.$
